newsitem.title: JAPAN: KDD aims for 40 bln yen group profit in 2000/01.
newsitem.headline: KDD aims for 40 bln yen group profit in 2000/01.

text.p: Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co (KDD) is aiming for a group current profit of 40 billion yen from its domestic and international services in the fiscal year ending on March 31, 2001, company president Tadashi Nishimoto told a news conference on Friday.

KDD plans to start domestic phone services, initially targeted at corporate users, in July following a revision of the law which governs KDD, which now bans the company from providing domestic services.
Nishimoto said KDD plans to start domestic long-distance services for individual consumers in early fiscal 1998/99 at "the most competitive rates".
Following the revision of the law, KDD said it will boost its capital spending for the current business year by 22 billion yen to 126 billion yen.
The company's parent current profit forecast for the current year remains unchanged at 17 billion yen, Nishimoto said.
Nishimoto said KDD hopes the government will do away with the KDD law, which includes restrictions on foreign ownership in KDD, as soon as possible.
"We hope to be fully privatised at least by the time NTT's restructuring is completed," he said.
Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp has said it plans to complete its restructuring by June 1999.
